anti_overlap: Leaves IndexedDB schema, migration version bumps, home-room/snapshot store persistence semantics, and multi-tab write races to the client-storage/migration reviewer.
Leaves canvas scale/DPR computation, integer pixel-scale rendering, image-smoothing scoping, offscreen snapshot capture, and viewport/camera-pan mechanics to the canvas-rendering reviewer.

Does not re-litigate whether roomFor's rotation weighting or the determinism sweep's existing mechanics are correct (Must-Have: mechanics are bit-identical) — reviews only the new tick-walk layer built on top of them.
decision_lens: If two Uncs' targets change under them while a third is mid-crossing and a fourth is waiting for a station, does the simulation still make guaranteed forward progress with no wall-clock leakage, or does it only work in the fixed, small scenario the plan's own tests construct?
focus: Whether the tick-based walk simulation (lib/houseWalk.ts, Task 4) and its wiring into the House rAF loop (Task 7 Step 1) actually produce deterministic, starvation-free, visually continuous figure movement as rooms are founded mid-session, home-room pull concentrates demand on one room, and browser frame timing is imperfect — or whether the plan's stated tests (Task 4 Step 4, AC 8) leave real deadlock, teleport, or fairness gaps unexercised.
name: fd-simsystems-tickwalk
persona: Apply the perspective of a systems engineer who has built and shipped real-time, tick-based agent simulations for colony-sim and RTS-style games — unit pathfinding on a graph of rooms/edges, station/slot capacity allocation, and deterministic-replay guarantees under imperfect frame timing.
review_areas: Task 4 Step 3 station/path assignment: what happens when a walker's path is invalidated mid-transit — a figure's roomByUnc target changes again before it finishes crossing (rotation ticks under it), or its destination room is removed from model.rooms between resolveHomeRooms cycles — does stepWalk recompute cleanly or can a walker get stuck referencing a stale room, door, or station?

Task 4 Step 3 ("if all stations are taken it waits at the door") combined with Task 7's "re-keyed by room set" initWalk reset on room-set change: verify a walk in progress (a figure mid-crossing a door or stair) survives a re-key rather than being reset every time a founding event fires initWalk again, and that founding a room mid-day doesn't visibly snap every walker back to a station.

Task 4 Step 4's 2,000-tick / 6-figure / 2-room stress test: check whether it actually exercises door-queue starvation — station capacity of 4 (STATIONS_PER_ROOM) versus more Uncs converging on one room once HOME_PULL (decision 6, Task 5) biases many Uncs toward the same home room — and whether the algorithm (not just the test) guarantees eventual progress once occupancy exceeds station capacity, since HOME_PULL can make that the common case rather than the edge case.

Determinism chain: key is injected per Task 4 Step 3 and AC 8 forbids performance.now/Date.now in houseWalk.ts, but Task 7's rAF loop ("accumulate elapsed, call stepWalk once per TICK_MS") lives in House.tsx, outside that grep — verify the accumulator can't drop or double-fire ticks under frame jank (backgrounded tab, slow device) in a way that changes the sequence of tick values fed into stepWalk, silently breaking the real-world determinism guarantee even though the unit test's "same key → deep-equal states" passes.

Idle bubble scheduling (Task 4 Step 3, f-030): "rolls a bubble only when no other walker in the same room has one" — with a single injected deterministic key, check whether this creates a persistent bias (the first-checked walker in a room always wins the roll) rather than fair rotation, and whether a figure that never gets a bubble across a whole session is an observable failure the plan's tests wouldn't catch (they check "at most one bubble per room," not distribution across figures).

Arrival/departure edge (f-019, f-022): the outside-to-porch-door walker, and figures "removed from the model leave via the porch door and are dropped when outside again" — verify a figure whose presence flips (rotation removes them) while mid-walk between two interior rooms is routed all the way back to the porch through valid doors and stairs rather than dropped or teleported from wherever it stood.

severity_examples.condition: A case the 2,000-tick/2-room test in Task 4 Step 4 never exercises, since it fixes figure count at 6 with no home-room bias applied.
severity_examples.scenario: resolveHomeRooms biases many Uncs toward the same home room (HOME_PULL) faster than the walk sim can move them out, so stations in that room stay permanently full; new arrivals to that room queue at its door forever because stepWalk's "wait at the door" branch has no eviction or overflow rule, freezing the simulation for that room every day the home-room pull is active.

severity_examples.condition: Founding happens on a normal cadence throughout a session (rooms are built as the ranch grows), so this is not a rare edge case.
severity_examples.scenario: initWalk is re-run "re-keyed by room set" (Task 7) whenever a room is founded, but the plan never states that in-flight walkers (mid-door, mid-stair) are carried over into the new WalkState; if initWalk simply restarts everyone at a station, founding a room while walkers are between rooms causes a visible full-house snap on every founding, undercutting the Must-Have that a walking figure is "visible the whole way."

severity_examples.condition: A quality regression from the intended ambient room life that Task 4 Step 4's tests would not catch, since they check "at most one bubble per room," not distribution across figures.
severity_examples.scenario: The bubble-fairness rule ("rolls a bubble only when no other walker in the same room has one") combined with a per-tick deterministic hash roll can let one station index win essentially every roll in a room with several occupants, so some figures are functionally silent for the whole session.

success_hints: Cites the specific Task 4 step, file anchor, or AC number (8, 9) it is testing against, not generic "concurrency is hard" claims.
Distinguishes a genuine deadlock/starvation/determinism gap in the algorithm as specified from a gap that is purely in the test coverage (Task 4 Step 4) — names which one for each finding.

Traces every finding through the actual data flow named in the plan (Task 7's walkRef/initWalk/stepWalk/register loop, Task 8's houseInput memo, resolveHomeRooms's effect trigger) rather than describing the walk sim in the abstract.

Treats "bit-identical mechanics" (rotation/residency untouched) as already covered by the determinism sweep and rotation tests; focuses only on the new tick-simulation layer's own correctness, not on re-verifying roomFor.

Leaves IndexedDB store shape, migration versioning, and snapshot capture timing to the persistence reviewer, and canvas draw-call/scale/DPR mechanics to the rendering reviewer — flags only where the walk state itself, not its visual rendering, is wrong.
